title: A lifelong mission call, after the children are cared for
setting: John Murdock joined the Church in Ohio in November 1830 and gave himself to preaching. His wife, Julia Clapp, died in April 1831 after giving birth to twins. Joseph and Emma Smith adopted the twins, and other families cared for his older children. One twin died in March 1832 after the mob attack on the Johnson home in Hiram. Murdock returned to Ohio sick that summer. Joseph Smith dictated this revelation for him at Hiram on 29 August 1832.
summary: The revelation calls John Murdock to preach in the eastern countries. He is to go from house to house, village to village, and city to city, amid persecution. Those who receive him receive the Lord, and he will speak with the power of the Spirit. Those who reject him will be rejected, and he is to cleanse his feet as a testimony against them. He is not to leave until his children are provided for and sent kindly to the bishop in Zion. After a few years he may go to Zion for his inheritance, if he wishes. Otherwise he is to keep preaching until he is taken.

contextNote.title: Family care comes before the mission
contextNote.text: Murdock was a widowed father whose children were scattered among other families. Verse 6 answers the obvious question: he must not leave until his children are provided for. The children are to be sent “kindly” to the bishop in Zion. Only then does the broad call of verse 1 take effect. Verses 7–8 then give him a choice between settling in Zion later or preaching for life. In this passage, provision for the children is a stated condition of the call, not an afterthought.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 98–101 includes this call to John Murdock, a father who sacrificed to serve. What do verses 2–3 promise Murdock as he preaches, and how might verse 6 shape how you balance service and family?
reviewNote: Read all 8 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, 29 August 1832, to John Murdock, and notes his wife’s death in April 1831. JSP historical introduction read for the twins’ adoption, Joseph Murdock Smith’s death in March 1832, the three older children sent to Zion, and Murdock leaving on 24 September 1832. The page rendered its title with blanks, so the JSP title is given in the site’s standard form; the URL was loaded. JSP reads “eastern countries” as long-settled eastern states such as New York. “Zion” mapped to independence. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes.
